svg.title: Line jumping on a timeline: the payload lands at tools/list
svg.desc: One session on a left-to-right timeline, across two lanes: the host with its client above, the server below. Six equally spaced steps. One, the client connects. Two, tools/list is sent. Three, in the lower lane, the server returns tool descriptions. Four, those descriptions enter the model context. Five, the user asks something and the model picks a tool. Six, the approval prompt is shown and only then is tools/call sent. Steps four and six are outlined in heavy ink; the rest are outlined in the client blue or the server terracotta. Below the axis, two bars measure the same clock. The first, hatched in red, starts at step four and runs to the end of the timeline, labelled payload resident in the model context. The second, plain and grey, starts at step six and is a fifth as long, labelled the approval prompt sees only this. A brace between the two start points is labelled the gap: two steps, and unbounded wall-clock time. Both bars are placed from the same table of step positions, so the difference in their lengths is measured rather than drawn. A panel at the bottom records that nothing in the sequence is malformed and a conformance suite passes all of it, that the injecting server's own tool is never called so it never appears in the interaction log, and that Trail of Bits in 2025 placed the attack before any tool is invoked, which is what puts it upstream of every gate.
svg.text: Line jumping: the payload lands at tools/list
Time runs left to right. Step 6 is the only point at which a human is asked anything.
payload resident in the model context
the approval prompt sees only this
the gap: two steps, and unbounded wall-clock time
Nothing here is malformed. Every message validates, and a conformance suite passes all of it.
The injecting server's own tool is never called, so it never appears in the interaction log.
Trail of Bits, 2025: the attack runs before any tool is invoked, which is what puts it upstream of every gate.
